scope.summary: This Indian Standard prescribes technical guidelines and methodology to develop functional testing procedures for evaluating electrical insulation systems (EIS) exposed to multiple co-existing aging factors (stresses) during their service life.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary National Code. However, state electricity boards, public works departments, and military equipment procurement agencies require high-voltage equipment, traction motors, and distribution transformers to carry test certificates demonstrating functional compliance with the multi-factor testing criteria of the IS 11182 series.

requirements.detail: Final observed or calculated test times, aging rates, specific stress limits, and statistical failure probabilities must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:2022 (second revision). The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in this standard.

Establishes definitions for aging interaction: the modification of the aging effect of one factor by the combination of two or more factors such that the combined effect differs significantly from the sum of their individual aging effects when acting independently.
Defines direct interaction as the interaction between simultaneously applied factors of influence that differs fundamentally from that occurring when those same factors are applied sequentially.
Defines indirect interaction as the interaction between simultaneously applied factors of influence that remains essentially unchanged when those same factors are applied sequentially.
Single-factor testing is technically valid and preferred only when interactions between service stress factors are absent or unknown.
Conducted on the same specimen batch in a repetitive loop of sequential steps. This approach is technically valid and highly practical when indirect interaction is present.
Simultaneous multi-factor testing is mandated when direct interaction is present. Stresses (e.g., heat, voltage, and vibration) must be applied to the specimen at the same physical instant.
Sequential procedures may be developed in which alternative consequential actions are listed to cover each possible outcome of a preceding action.

Where service relationships and aging interactions are not confidently known, technical committees or manufacturers must instigate research to identify specific aging factors, their relative importance, and their physical interactions.

During testing, if there are no failures, or an insufficient number of failures within the planned number of test cycles, engineers must either continue testing cycles until a sufficient number of failures occur or carry out additional diagnostic tests to reveal the extent of deterioration.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 11182 (Part 7/Sec 1) : 1986 (Reaffirmed 2021) is the primary national Indian Standard code of practice prescribing procedures for multi-factor functional testing of electrical insulation systems. Technically equivalent to international standard IEC TR 60792-1:1985 and modernly consolidated under IEC 60505, the standard unifies how electrical, thermal, mechanical, and environmental stresses are combined to simulate real-world service aging. It defines crucial concepts like aging interaction and provides a logical decision matrix to choose between separate single-factor tests, sequential tests on the same specimen, and complex simultaneous tests. Incorporating rigid failure evaluation guidelines, the code outlines alternative diagnostic procedures when planned test cycles yield insufficient failures, ensuring high-voltage windings and motors achieve optimal reliability and occupant safety.
